questions.question: What is the basic structure of a pinhole camera?
options: A tube with a curved mirror at one end and an eyepiece at the other.
An empty, closed box with a tiny hole on the front face and a screen on the back face.
A sealed glass cylinder containing a gas that glows when light passes through it.
A double-lens system with a converging lens at the front and a diverging lens at the back.

questions.question: How does light travel from a light source, through the pinhole, to the screen in a pinhole camera?
options: It moves in straight lines.
It curves gradually towards the center of the box.
It bounces off the internal walls before reaching the screen.
It bends sharply at the entrance of the pinhole.

questions.question: What happens to the image formed by a pinhole camera if you poke a second, separate hole next to the first one?
options: The single image becomes twice as bright.
The single image becomes upright instead of inverted.
Multiple images are produced on the screen.
No image is formed at all because the light rays cancel out.

questions.question: What is the effect of making the hole in a pinhole camera larger?
options: The image becomes sharper but much dimmer.
The image becomes brighter but blurred.
The image becomes inverted and smaller.
The image becomes upright but highly distorted.

questions.question: Which part of a lens receives light from any given point on an object?
options: Only the very outer edges of the lens.
Only the central point of the lens.
Some light from every point on an object passes through every part of the lens.
Only the top half of the lens receives light from the top half of the object.

questions.question: What is the name given to the point where light rays meet after being refracted and brought closer together by a convex lens?
options: The normal.
The reflection.
The focus.
The dispersion.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the size and orientation of an image reflected in a flat plane mirror?
options: It is twice the size of the object and upside down.
It is smaller than the object and upright.
It is the same size as the object and upright.
It is larger than the object and inverted.

questions.question: If you face a plane mirror, how does your reflection appear compared to your actual body?
options: Upside down.
Magnified and distorted.
Laterally inverted.
Unchanged and perfectly identical without any inversion.

questions.question: Why are reflections in a plane mirror described as virtual images?
options: They appear where light rays seem to have come from, not where they actually come from.
They can be projected directly onto a physical screen placed behind the mirror.
They only exist when we close our eyes and imagine them.
They are created by light rays that actually converge at a single physical point.

questions.question: What determines the colour of an object when it is illuminated by white or coloured light?
options: The speed at which light passes completely through the solid object.
The amounts of red, green, and blue light it is reflecting.
The total thermal energy absorbed by the outer surface of the object.
The distance between the light source and the object's surface.

questions.question: Why does a black object appear black under white light?
options: It absorbs all colours of light.
It reflects only red and green light.
It refracts all incoming light at a very sharp angle.
It transmits all light directly through its center.

questions.question: What direction does a ray of light turn when it enters a transparent material from air at an angle?
options: It turns away from the normal.
It turns towards the normal.
It continues in a perfectly straight line without changing direction.
It reflects directly backward along its original path.

questions.question: What happens to a light ray that enters and leaves a glass block with parallel sides?
options: It is bent permanently at a 90-degree angle to its original path.
It ends up in its original direction, but displaced to the side.
It is completely absorbed and turned into heat energy.
It is split into a circular rainbow pattern without exiting the block.

questions.question: What is produced when you mix equal amounts of red, green, and blue light?
options: Black light.
Yellow light.
White light.
Magenta light.

questions.question: How do display screens produce a wide range of different colours?
options: By using tiny filters that physically slide across a single white light bulb.
By using tiny red, green, and blue lights (pixels) that vary in brightness.
By changing the chemical composition of the screen glass in real time.
By vibrating the screen at different high frequencies.

questions.question: Which object can be used to split up sunlight into a visible light spectrum?
options: A flat piece of opaque cardboard.
A transparent triangular prism.
A highly polished metal plane mirror.
A concave magnifying lens.
